art_instructions: From a child’s eye level, show a cozy Greek classroom with a soft blue wall, a large sunlit window at left, and a honey-oak student desk on the right over a small woven rug with simple geometric patterns. In the foreground, the Owl (chibi style, mottled brown-and-cream feathers, round amber eyes, small green scarf) sits beside the desk on a low honey-oak stool, not tucked under it, her round body angled slightly toward the desktop. Place the Owl on the left-center of the frame and the desk on the right-center, close enough that her left wing can lightly touch the desk’s edge, clearly showing she sits by the desk. She is about two-thirds the height of the desk, feet tucked in, wings relaxed on her lap, with a calm, attentive smile as if ready to learn. Hang her tiny satchel from the desk leg or a small peg on the side of the desk, with a couple of picture cards peeking out; avoid any writing. Background details stay simple: a low teacher podium and two more small desks recede softly, a potted green plant near the window, and warm natural light pooling on the rug. Use the Korean aegyo cute style with rounded silhouettes, flat pastels and a brighter green accent on the scarf, minimal soft cel-shading, and clean monoline strokes; fill the frame edge to edge with this airy classroom.
